statusDetail: Coverage-complete agentic audit across five representative paths.

page.framework: React-like hybrid with legacy/global Microsoft components
page.notes: Public localized commerce/media site. Covered landing, catalog, product, subscription, and error archetypes. Authenticated checkout/account, cloud play, support, accessibility hub, and post-purchase flows were not covered because they require authentication or are separate template families beyond this run.

paths.description: Homepage and global navigation, representing the primary landing experience.
Console game catalog, representing listing, filtering, pricing, and browse-to-detail discovery.
Xbox Series X detail page, representing a product detail and purchase-intent journey.
Game Pass page, representing subscription comparison and join intent.
Deliberate invalid route, representing HTTP/navigation recovery.

findings.summary: The site does not adapt to the system dark-color preference.
findings.evidence: The dark-emulated screenshot is pixel-identical in appearance and byte size to the default capture; the DOM reports color-scheme: normal and the consent/header surfaces remain white.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and provide prefers-color-scheme-driven surface, text, and control tokens, using light-dark() where appropriate.

findings.summary: Navigation and state changes do not expose a View Transition treatment.
findings.evidence: DOM/CSS inspection found no view-transition styling while the representative journey is composed of full document links and carousel/state swaps.
findings.suggestedFix: Add progressive cross-document View Transitions for same-origin navigation and same-document transitions for carousel/state changes, respecting reduced motion.

findings.summary: The cookie notice dominates the initial viewport before users can reach Xbox content.
findings.evidence: Desktop and mobile screenshots show the notice consuming roughly 336px and 344px respectively; on mobile it occupies over 40% of the first viewport.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce the initial consent treatment to a compact, accessible notice that preserves equally prominent reject/manage controls without obscuring the primary content.

findings.summary: The load-time consent overlay is not represented by a dialog or other semantic overlay primitive.
findings.evidence: The DOM probe found zero dialog elements and the targeted DOM capture found no [role=dialog], despite the visually dominant consent surface.
findings.suggestedFix: Model the notice with the appropriate dialog semantics, labelled description, predictable focus handling, and declarative close behavior.

findings.summary: A material set of interactive targets is smaller than the minimum practical target size.
findings.evidence: The focus/target probe counted 25 visible links, buttons, or inputs below 24px in at least one dimension. Lighthouse still scored automated accessibility at 100, so this is a modality/target-size gap rather than a broad a11y failure.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase the clickable area around compact icon and pagination controls to at least 24x24 CSS px, preferably 44x44 where layout permits.

findings.summary: The mobile load is slow and severely unstable.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured performance 13, LCP 23.7s, TBT 740ms, and CLS 0.761. Raw layout captures reproduced CLS from 0.441 to 0.901 across all four representative templates.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the hero/LCP image, reserve all media and consent/header geometry, shorten critical chains, and defer nonessential JavaScript.

findings.summary: Unsized images and late UI cause major layout shifts.
findings.evidence: The image audit found all 43 images lacked width/height attributes. Lighthouse attributed the CLS 0.761 shifts to unsized Microsoft and content images; per-template layout captures reached CLS 0.901.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit intrinsic width and height or aspect-ratio for every image and reserve stable space for consent/header and lazy content.

findings.summary: Mobile execution blocks interactivity during load.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured 740ms total blocking time and a 560ms maximum potential input delay. Layout observations also recorded 56-101ms long tasks on representative pages.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove unnecessary startup work, split remaining long tasks, and schedule noncritical work after content and interaction readiness.

findings.summary: The critical hero is discovered late and the page ships an oversized dependency chain.
findings.evidence: The HAR recorded 140 requests and 8,556,801 transferred bytes. Lighthouse found the LCP request not discoverable in initial HTML, no fetchpriority=high, and a longest critical chain of 8.58s.
findings.suggestedFix: Make the LCP image discoverable in server HTML, set fetchpriority=high, remove noncritical resources from startup, and preconnect only to high-value origins.

findings.summary: Large amounts of shipped CSS and JavaScript are unused on the audited route.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated savings of 585KiB unused JavaScript and 560KiB unused CSS; the HAR shows 51 scripts and 15 stylesheets.
findings.suggestedFix: Route-split legacy and modern page bundles, remove duplicate framework/global-share styles, and conditionally load consent, account, and merchandising code.

findings.summary: Product and subscription templates contain repeated top-level headings and empty headings.
findings.evidence: The console probe found six H1 elements all reading “XBOX SERIES X”; Game Pass found three H1s and multiple empty H3s. This conflicts with the otherwise strong Lighthouse/axe accessibility results.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep one page H1, demote duplicated responsive/visual variants out of the accessibility tree, and remove or name empty headings.

findings.summary: Deprecated APIs, a BFCache blocker, and broken source maps remain in production.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found unload listeners, synchronous XHR, nonstandard slider-vertical CSS, BFCache prevention, and multiple missing/404 source maps.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove unload handlers and synchronous XHR, replace slider-vertical usage, and publish valid maps or remove stale sourceMappingURL references.

findings.summary: The console-games listing lacks a meta description.
findings.evidence: The listing probe returned a descriptive title and canonical URL but no meta description, while the other representative pages provided one.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a unique description summarizing the console catalog and its browse/filter value.

findings.summary: Important browser security headers are absent and cookies use a broad cross-site posture.
findings.evidence: The headers primitive found no Content-Security-Policy, Referrer-Policy, or Permissions-Policy. All four observed first-party cookies used SameSite=None, although HTTPS, HSTS, nosniff, and X-Frame-Options were present.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy an enforcing CSP, strict referrer and permissions policies, and narrow cookies to Lax/Strict unless a documented cross-site flow requires None.

findings.summary: The landing page has a broad third-party and telemetry footprint before interaction.
findings.evidence: The tracker primitive observed 15 third-party origins, including 20 requests to Adobe DTM and 10 telemetry requests to browser.events.data.microsoft.com. Lighthouse observed nine third-party cookies.
findings.suggestedFix: Gate optional analytics until consent, consolidate telemetry, reduce partner origins, and document the value and retention of each remaining call.

findings.summary: Defensive policy coverage is incomplete despite good HSTS and clickjacking protection.
findings.evidence: Headers show HSTS, nosniff and X-Frame-Options DENY, but no CSP/frame-ancestors policy, Referrer-Policy, or Permissions-Policy.
findings.suggestedFix: Add CSP with frame-ancestors and Trusted Types where feasible, plus explicit Referrer-Policy and least-privilege Permissions-Policy.

findings.summary: The homepage exposes only a minority of its rendered content to non-JavaScript clients.
findings.evidence: Discoverability comparison found only 30% rendered-word coverage in raw HTML and no raw H1, versus 95% coverage for the console detail template. The homepage is not an empty shell, but its primary merchandising content is substantially JS-dependent.
findings.suggestedFix: Server-render the homepage heading, hero copy, and primary destination links, then hydrate enhancements without replacing core content.

findings.summary: Image delivery is heavier and less modern than the experience requires.
findings.evidence: The image audit found 30 legacy-format images, 7 oversized images, 6 below-fold images not lazy-loaded, and all 43 without dimensions. Images accounted for 5,655,392 of 8,556,801 transferred bytes.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve AVIF/WebP variants at display-appropriate sizes, lazy-load below-fold imagery, preserve responsive srcsets, and set intrinsic dimensions.

findings.summary: The initial page budget is dominated by media and a large multi-origin dependency graph.
findings.evidence: The HAR transferred 8.56MB across 140 requests; images were 5.66MB and the tracker probe found 15 third-party origins.
findings.suggestedFix: Set route-specific transfer budgets, defer below-fold campaigns and third parties, and stop background telemetry from competing with core media.

findings.summary: The homepage starts with a large in-memory object and DOM footprint.
findings.evidence: The baseline heap summary contained 740,542 nodes, 2,571,691 edges, and 45.9MB self size. Repeated scrolling did not increase it, so this is footprint rather than demonstrated leakage.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile the largest retained constructors, reduce duplicated/hidden campaign DOM, and defer modules that are not needed in the current viewport.

taskList.title: Fix LCP, CLS, request weight, and image delivery
Shrink and semantically rebuild the consent surface
Deploy complete browser security and privacy policies
Repair heading structure and compact target sizes
Remove deprecated runtime patterns and stale source maps
